messages.author: 751017d3d583ea2e
messages.subject: Unhandled Exception: HTTP 599: Timeout
parts:
Hi, 

I faced a "HTTP 599: Timeout" error when I tried to deploy my Shiny app. I tried different R versions but that did not seem to help.

I have a large number of files (~2.7G) and I did set the followings to allow for more files:

options(rsconnect.max.bundle.size=3145728000)
options(rsconnect.max.bundle.files=50000)

When I retried with only a few files the deployment worked successfully. So could this really be a timeout error as it was taking too long to install the files? How can I fix this?

Appreciate any help! Thank you!

messages.author: 299a5089d6c6c523
messages.subject: Re: Unhandled Exception: HTTP 599: Timeout
parts:
A checksum is computed locally for each file uploaded, and then when the uploaded bundle is extracted those checksums are checked.
The more files in the bundle, the longer that takes. 
Since this is more a function of the number of files, than of size, you can work around this by putting files into a .zip or .tar file and having your application expand it when it starts. Obviously this advice applies only to data files and not to the application source itself.
HTH.

parts: Hi Joshua, I did as you suggested and my problem was solved immediately! Can't thank you enough!

On Thursday, February 8, 2018 at 9:17:12 AM UTC-8, Joshua Spiewak wrote:
A checksum is computed locally for each file uploaded, and then when the uploaded bundle is extracted those checksums are checked.
The more files in the bundle, the longer that takes. 
Since this is more a function of the number of files, than of size, you can work around this by putting files into a .zip or .tar file and having your application expand it when it starts. Obviously this advice applies only to data files and not to the application source itself.
HTH.

On Wednesday, February 7, 2018 at 3:28:41 PM UTC-5, YWL wrote:
Hi, 

I faced a "HTTP 599: Timeout" error when I tried to deploy my Shiny app. I tried different R versions but that did not seem to help.

I have a large number of files (~2.7G) and I did set the followings to allow for more files:

options(rsconnect.max.bundle.size=3145728000)
options(rsconnect.max.bundle.files=50000)

When I retried with only a few files the deployment worked successfully. So could this really be a timeout error as it was taking too long to install the files? How can I fix this?

Appreciate any help! Thank you!
